hints: Focus on which bond in a CFC is most easily broken by UV light in the stratosphere.
Remember that the C-Cl bond breaks to give $\text{Cl}^\bullet$, while the C-F bond is much stronger and stays intact.
Think about which radical acts as a catalyst to destroy ozone and is regenerated, and check which of statements 1, 2 and 3 fits that role.
walkthrough:
**See what UV does to a CFC**

UV radiation causes homolytic fission of the weakest bond in the molecule. In chlorofluoroalkanes, that is the C-Cl bond.

$$\text{CFCl}_3 \xrightarrow{UV} \text{ }^\bullet\text{CFCl}_2 + \text{Cl}^\bullet$$

**Spot the ozone-destroying catalyst**

The chlorine radical is the dangerous one. It reacts with ozone and is then regenerated, so one $\text{Cl}^\bullet$ can destroy thousands of $\text{O}_3$ molecules.

$$\text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{ClO}^\bullet + \text{O}_2$$
$$\text{ClO}^\bullet + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Cl}^\bullet + 2\text{O}_2$$

**Rule out the other radicals**

The C-F bond is very strong and is not broken by this UV, so $\text{F}^\bullet$ is not formed in significant amounts. Even if formed, fluorine is quickly trapped as very stable HF and does not catalyse ozone loss. The alkyl fragment $\text{ }^\bullet\text{CFCl}_2$ is quickly removed by other reactions and does not destroy ozone. So only statement 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This implies 1, 2 and 3 are all ozone-depleting radicals. Only chlorine radicals have the correct catalytic cycle. Fluorine radicals are not released and alkyl radicals do not destroy ozone.
options.B: Incorrect. This implies 1 and 2 are correct. While 1 is correct, 2 is wrong because the C-F bond ($\approx$ 467 kJ mol-1) is much stronger than C-Cl and is not cleaved. Fluorine ends up as unreactive HF, not as a chain carrier.
options.C: Incorrect. This implies 2 and 3 are correct and 1 is wrong. This is backwards. Chlorine radicals are the proven catalyst for ozone depletion, while neither fluorine nor alkyl radicals carry out this catalytic destruction.
options.D: Correct. This implies only 1 is correct. UV breaks C-Cl to release $\text{Cl}^\bullet$, which catalytically converts $\text{O}_3$ to $\text{O}_2$ and is regenerated to continue the chain.
